{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABYfH9zg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhCDXI4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 3, "title": "Implement the first browser-runnable Rust/Wasm prototype with three WonderSwan models", "body": "## Problem

The repository has contribution guidance but no emulator implementation or buildable application. Starting with CPU, graphics, audio, and game compatibility all at once would make the first change too large to validate.

We need the **smallest runnable end-to-end foundation** for a from-scratch WonderSwan emulator: a platform-independent Rust core, a WebAssembly bridge, and a browser UI that demonstrably communicate. The user must be able to choose among **WonderSwan, WonderSwan Color, and SwanCrystal**, with **SwanCrystal selected by default**.

This Issue defines an **initial, non-playable prototype**, not a promise of commercial game compatibility. Later Issues will implement V30MZ CPU execution, address/bus mapping, video timing, input, audio, and accurate hardware differences.

## Expected outcome

Running the documented local development command opens a browser page that:

1. Displays a 224 × 144 pixel canvas whose RGBA framebuffer originates in the Rust core through WebAssembly.
2. Offers exactly three console model choices: **WonderSwan (mono)**, **WonderSwan Color**, and **SwanCrystal (default)**.
3. Creates/resets the Rust machine for the selected model. The model shown in the UI reflects the model held by the Rust core, not just a JavaScript-only selection.
4. Lets the user select a **local ROM file** and passes its bytes into the Rust/Wasm core. It reports the selected filename and the byte count accepted by the core.
5. Clearly explains that **ROM bytes are loaded but games cannot run yet**. There is no misleading Start/Play action or claim that hardware compatibility is implemented.

The deliverable is a reproducible local development baseline on which independent implementers can build actual emulation components.

## Context and implementation scope

- Repository: `takahirox/wonderswan-rust`, default branch `main`.
- Follow [development flow](../blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](../blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), and [AI guidance](../blob/main/AGENTS.md). Write source Issue, PR, documentation, and commits in English.
- Implement the emulator **from scratch in Rust**. Hardware specifications and instruction-set documentation may be consulted, but do **not** copy, port, vendor, or depend on an existing emulator implementation.
- Keep the emulator core independent of browser APIs and JavaScript. Expose it through a thin WebAssembly adapter, with a minimal TypeScript browser frontend. A Cargo workspace with separate core and Wasm crates is suggested (e.g. `crates/ws-core` and `crates/ws-web`); the exact file layout may vary if equivalently simple.
- Define an explicit model type (for example, `Mono`, `Color`, `Crystal`) and make `Crystal` the default in the core as well as the UI. Record model identity in machine state so subsequent hardware differences can be implemented without three independent emulator codebases.
- Model selection **resets/recreates** the machine and clears the previously loaded ROM (the user may load it again). The status display must reflect the reset.
- The core should accept arbitrary nonempty byte buffers as **raw cartridge data** for now and report their stored length; reject empty data with a clear recoverable error. Do **not** attempt incomplete ROM-header validation, cartridge mapping, booting, or compatibility detection in this Issue.
- Define a framebuffer of **224 × 144 RGBA pixels**, expose its bytes to the WebAssembly adapter, and display it through a browser canvas using nearest-neighbor/pixelated scaling. A deterministic blank/clear framebuffer is sufficient: **do not fabricate game graphics or LCD hardware simulation**.
- ROM selection must read a local file in-browser (no upload endpoint, server-side ROM storage, bundled copyrighted ROMs, or external downloads).
- Provide the minimum build/development tooling and README instructions required to build/test the Rust core, build its Wasm bridge, install frontend dependencies, and launch/build the frontend. Avoid unrelated scaffolding, frameworks, or CI changes.
- Keep the core API minimal; it needs only construction/model inspection, model reset/selection, ROM-byte loading/status, and framebuffer access for this slice.

### Explicitly out of scope

Actual V30MZ instruction execution, boot ROM behavior, memory-bank mapping, interrupts, timers, scanline rendering, palette accuracy, sound, keypad emulation, save states, persistent storage, ROM format compatibility checking, game playback, and differences in physical LCD appearance. Those belong in focused follow-up Issues.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Rust workspace builds with a browser-independent emulator core and a thin WebAssembly adapter. The frontend uses TypeScript and works in a modern browser without a backend.
- [ ] The core represents all three named console models and defaults to SwanCrystal. Selecting another model updates the actual Rust machine state, resets it, and clears previously loaded ROM data.
- [ ] The browser UI initially selects SwanCrystal, can select the other two models, and displays the currently active model reported by the Rust core.
- [ ] The browser accepts a local nonempty file, passes the **actual file bytes** to WebAssembly, and displays the correct accepted byte count. An empty file and file-reading errors are reported without crashing the UI.
- [ ] A 224 × 144 RGBA framebuffer owned/generated by the Rust core is rendered to the browser canvas; resizing its CSS display does not change the internal resolution or blur its pixels.
- [ ] The UI clearly states the prototype **does not execute ROMs or play games yet**; loading a ROM never pretends a game is running.
- [ ] Automated Rust unit tests cover: default model; selection of all three models; reset clearing ROM state; successful byte loading/byte count; rejection of empty input; framebuffer dimensions and byte length.
- [ ] The README states the project's from-scratch intent, three-model target with SwanCrystal default, exactly what the prototype does and does not do, prerequisites, and **actual reproducible commands** for Rust tests, Wasm compilation, local browser development, and frontend production build.
- [ ] Run and report the actual results of Rust tests, Wasm compilation, and frontend production build before requesting merge. Also verify a local browser smoke flow (default model → select Mono/Color/Crystal → load nonempty file → reset/switch → reject empty file) and report how it was checked. Do not claim an unperformed check passed.
- [ ] Changes are limited to the smallest coherent foundation for this Issue; no emulator dependencies, unrelated abstractions, or speculative systems.

## Optional validation

- Use a small original dummy file to manually verify that no bytes leave the browser during ROM selection.
- Exercise the local demo on another browser or device if available; this is not a merge blocker.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Building and exercising the local application are pre-merge checks; no deployed site or release is required for this Issue.
